To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the novel allergen‐carrying and adjuvating complex CBP–rFeld1 induces the up‐regulation in the expression of the CD86 costimulatory molecule on MDDCs and enhances the release of proinflammatory cytokines by MDDCs in vitro.

a novel adjuvant‐allergen complex (carbohydrate‐based particle–recombinant Fel d 1), which induces up‐regulates of CD86 and enhanced cytokine release by dendritic cells, may be useful for improving the effectiveness of allergen‐ specific immunotherapy.

a novel allergen–adjuvant complex, consisting of a recombinant major allergen and a carbohydrate‐based particle, enhances the expression of the co‐stimulatory molecule CD86 and the release of pro‐inflammatory cytokines by human dendritic cell in vitro.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel allergen delivery systems for the improvement of specific immunotherapy.
the development and evaluation of novel adjuvants for the improvement of immunotherapy.
the development of a new allergen carrier, carbohydrate‐based particles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this is a promising candidate adjuvant that can be used in immunotherapy.

the CBPs have the potential to be a novel allergen carrier and/or adjuvant in allergen‐specific treatment of allergic diseases, such as asthma and allergic rhinitis, as a result of their capacity to induce a Th1 response and to induce the expression of the co‐stimulatory molecule, CD 86.
the use of carbohydrate‐based particles as an allergen‐specific adjuvant is promising and should be further investigated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of carbohydrate‐based particles as an allergen adjuvant may be a promising candidate for improving allergen‐specific therapy.
we have developed an improved method for immunotherapy, where the carrier and adjuvants have been combined.
the use of carbohydrate‐based particles as an allergen delivery system and adjuvant for immunotherapy is promising.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the carbohydrate‐based particles, CBPs, are a promising candidate for allergen‐specific immuno therapy.
the use of a carbohydrate‐based particle as an allergen adjuvant is promising.
the use of carbohydrate‐based particles as a carrier for allergens and an adjuvant for immunotherapy is promising.
